summary: Allegany County, MD 80-foot forestry tower on Town Hill, installed 1931 for state forest protection; 2007 state report calls it sound and a communications site; FFLA lists it standing.

facts.design: 80-foot forestry tower with a cab and stairs, within a fenced communications compound
facts.agency: Maryland DNR Forest Service (managing agency); site on Green Ridge State Forest land

access.note: Tower sits in a fenced communications compound on state forest land, reached from Mountain Road north of U.S. Route 40; DNR records the current use as a communications site

events.note: Fourth tower erected that summer on the crest of Town Hill, 80 feet high (1931 newspaper); DNR gives the installation date as 1931
State took the site by deed, 12 November 1931
DNR report (April 2007, towers as of December 2006) found the tower structurally sound with cab and stairs in good repair

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1931 newspaper gives 1,760 feet for the crest; the 2007 DNR report gives a base elevation of 1,685 feet. The two figures are not reconciled, so no elevation is recorded.

sources.title: Forestry Towers and Forestry Tower Properties: A Resource Document

notes_for_editor: The DNR report is dated April 2007 and covers towers managed as of December 2006, so the condition finding is roughly 20 years old. FFLA lists the tower as standing with no asterisk, which fits the report. The DNR table gives 80 feet and a good condition. The 1,760 versus 1,685 foot elevation gap is left open. No staffing record or visiting policy was found; the DNR report describes the site as a fenced communications compound, so access is set to restricted. Do not encourage climbing.
